This is a really interesting question. When it comes to the internet’s role in this, I think that a lot of it is just a byproduct of the nature of social media.

Before the rise of Web 2.0, most socialization on the internet took place in closed, individually-run moderated areas like newsgroups, forums, etc. These places were dedicated to a single topic and somebody had the job of keeping them free of spam and off-topic junk, so for the most part, you weren’t aware of everyone’s personal baggage outside of the community. Every group had its crazy members, but for the most part, their irrelevent craziness tended to be kept to a minimum.

But the rise of social media has changed how we view content: We join large, aggregate sites (like Twitter, Tumblr, Facebook, etc.) to follow individuals and read a “feed” of everything they post. The only real organization to it is having “tags” that are specified by users at their own discretion, with nobody to clean up the off-topic crap.

The end result of this is that the people who feed on anger and drama now have an ample supply, while it’s getting harder and harder for the rest of us to just go about our business without being subject to everyone else’s pet causes.

Ctrl+Z (pauses job)

bg (puts it in the background and unpauses)

jobs (checks that it's running in the background)

I may be a bit late but the reason for the program dying is due to your session being killed when you close terminal. There is disadvantages to ctrl-z and thats in some cases say if its calling another script that runs another session then it will still die. Nohup will help with that. I personally use screen. Its the greatest thing since sliced bread for running apps and forgetting about them.

Because it was designed that way since the time when terminals were actual terminals, used to connect to mainframes. Most programs have no need to run when the user isn't interacting with them, especially the shell. Therefore all programs get a signal (the hang-up signal, SIGHUP) when their controlling terminal dies and most of them will die in response.

In addition to bg (or detach), screen and tmux I can suggest running programs as command &! which will start them in detached state.
